## What's new

- **Saving always saves the map.** When the map's tile libraries changed, DS1 Studio used to update LvlTypes.txt and the Dt1Mask (LvlPrest.txt) first, and a problem there (for example, a level type with all 32 slots used) stopped the map from being saved. Now the map is written first and the tables after. If they can't be updated, the save still goes through and you're told why.
- **New preference: "Update LvlTypes / Dt1Mask when saving"** (Preferences → Saving; on by default). Turn it off to keep saving to the map only and edit the tables yourself. The Compatibility check shows what the game won't load.
- **When a level type is full**, a dialog opens. It appears after saving, after adding libraries, or from the Compatibility check's "Update LvlTypes automatically" fix, and offers three ways out:
  1. **Remove libraries nothing uses.** These are slots no map of the level type selects in its Dt1Mask. The rest move up with no gaps, and every map's Dt1Mask is renumbered to match. This is only offered when all of the type's levels are preset levels.
  2. **Combine some of the map's DT1s into one.** Their tiles are copied, in load order, into a new DT1 that takes one slot. The map looks the same, because the game pools the tiles of every library it loads anyway. Slots only this map used are freed; the original DT1s stay for other maps. The dialog shows whether the result fits.
  3. **Change level type…** gives the level a type of its own.
- A level type shared with other levels that is full now gives this level a type of its own when it needs a new library, as it already did when the type had room, instead of failing.
